title: Ansible Ad-Hoc Commands - System Administration and File Management

lab_objective.description: By the end of this lab, students should be able to:
objectives: Create a group with the group module.
Create a user with the user module, then add that user to the group in a separate task.
Install a package with the dnf module.
Start a service and enable it at boot in separate tasks.
Add a firewall rule to allow the service.
Use the shell module to collect system information and save it to a file.
Create directories and files with the file module.
Create a file with content using the copy module and copy it to a different filename.
Create a nested directory structure and copy a directory.
lab_objective.scenario: You are a Linux administrator using an Ansible control node to configure one or more RHEL-family managed nodes. Complete each task with an Ansible ad-hoc command. Unless a task says otherwise, run the command against the dev inventory group. Use privilege escalation where required.
prerequisites: An Ansible control node is configured and can connect to the managed nodes.
The inventory file is /etc/ansible/hosts and contains a [dev] group with at least one reachable RHEL-family managed node.
The remote account can use sudo, and the ad-hoc commands can use --become when administrative privileges are required.
Managed nodes use DNF and systemd, and firewalld is installed and running.
The managed nodes can access configured package repositories.

tasks.title: Verify connectivity to managed nodes
steps: Use the ping module to verify that Ansible can connect to every host in the dev group.
Make sure you will Perform all tasks on dev host group only.

tasks.title: Create the devsecops group
steps: Use the group module to create a group named devsecops on the managed nodes.
Ensure the group exists with the appropriate state.

tasks.title: Create the user
steps: Use the user module to create a user named deployer.
Create the user without assigning any secondary group in this task.
Ensure the user account exists.

tasks.title: Add the user to the group
steps: In a separate ad-hoc command, use the user module to add deployer to the devsecops supplementary group.
Use append behavior so that existing supplementary group memberships are preserved.

tasks.title: Install the Apache web server package
steps: Use the dnf module to install the httpd package.
Ensure the package is present on the managed nodes.

tasks.title: Start the Apache service
steps: Use the service module to start the httpd service.
Keep this as a separate task from enabling the service.

tasks.title: Enable Apache at boot
steps: Use the service module to enable the httpd service so it starts automatically at boot.

tasks.title: Collect system information with the shell module and save to a file
steps: Use the shell module to collect the managed node kernel version, mounted file systems, and memory in human readable form.
Redirect the information into /tmp/ansible-system-info.txt on each managed node.

tasks.title: Create a working directory
steps: Use the file module to create the directory /opt/ansible-lab.
Ensure it is a directory and that it exists.

tasks.title: Create an empty file in the directory
steps: Use the file module to create an empty file named notes.txt inside /opt/ansible-lab.
Ensure the file exists and is a regular file.

tasks.title: Create a file with content using the copy module
steps: Use the copy module to create /opt/ansible-lab/announcement.txt.
Set the file content to: Ansible ad-hoc commands can automate routine Linux administration tasks.

tasks.title: Copy a file with a different name
steps: Use the copy module to copy /opt/ansible-lab/announcement.txt to /opt/ansible-lab/announcement-backup.txt.
Preserve the file content in the destination file.

tasks.title: Create a nested directory structure
steps: Use the file module to create /opt/ansible-lab/reports/weekly/archive.
Create the full directory structure in one ad-hoc command.

tasks.title: Create a source directory and files
steps: Use the file module to create /opt/ansible-lab/source-dir.
Use the copy module to create a file named source.txt inside that directory with the content: This file is used to practice directory copying

tasks.title: Copy a directory
steps: Use the copy module to copy the directory /opt/ansible-lab/source-dir to /opt/ansible-lab/source-dir-copy.
Specify the source directory without a trailing slash so the source-dir directory itself is copied into the destination.
Remember that the copy module copies directory contents recursively by default; it does not require a recursive parameter.

completion_message: Lab 402 completed. You practiced Ansible ad-hoc commands for user and group management, package and service administration, firewall configuration, system information collection, and file and directory operations.
